requirement: Describe a Phase 3, multicenter, open-label, single-arm fixed-dose-titration study of once-daily NBI-98854 for long-term safety and tolerability in tardive dyskinesia; do not imply randomization or a concurrent control.

evidence.text: The cover and synopsis identify Phase 3, open-label fixed-dose titration and approximately 50 sites; every participant receives NBI-98854.

requirement: Represent dosing as 40 mg once daily through Week 4, optional investigator-directed escalation to 80 mg when response and tolerability criteria permit, and reduction back to 40 mg after escalation when 80 mg is not tolerated.

evidence.text: The synopsis defines starting dose, Week-4 escalation criteria and subsequent dose reduction.

requirement: Use a 48-week treatment period followed by a Week-52 visit four weeks after the last dose, with scheduled treatment visits every four weeks and the protocol's plus-or-minus-six-day visit window.

evidence.text: The synopsis gives the treatment, follow-up, visit schedule and visit window.

requirement: Define the target population as medically and psychiatrically stable adults aged 18 through 85 with moderate or severe neuroleptic-induced tardive dyskinesia and schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or a mood disorder.
acceptable_values: schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder

evidence.text: The study-population synopsis gives age, diagnosis, severity and stability requirements.

requirement: State that the planned sample size was approximately 180 participants based on practical considerations, not a statistical power calculation; do not invent a treatment-effect assumption or confirmatory power target.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the approximate enrollment and explicitly says the sample size is not based on formal power calculations.
The SAP confirms a practical rather than power-based sample size.

requirement: Use one safety analysis set containing enrolled participants dispensed study drug, excluding those who return every dispensed dose unused and those with no postbaseline data; base all summaries except enrollment, disposition, site enrollment and set membership on this set.

evidence.text: Section 5.8 defines the sole analysis set, its two exclusions and its binding to summaries.

requirement: Summarize postbaseline data by observed dose trajectory—40 mg, 80 mg, 80/40 mg and overall—and assign participants discontinuing before Week 4 to 40 mg; identify these as nonrandomized descriptive groups, not causal treatment arms.

evidence.text: Section 5.1 defines dose-trajectory groups and the pre-Week-4 discontinuation rule.

requirement: Pool study sites for every table and graph except the subject-enrollment-by-site summary because most sites are expected to enroll fewer than five participants.

evidence.text: Section 5.4 prespecifies site pooling and the sole exception.

requirement: Map qualifying early-termination observations to Week 4 for study days 21-34, to Weeks 8-48 within each SAP-defined minus-14/plus-13-day window, and to Week 52 from study day 350 onward; list but exclude unmapped observations from by-visit summaries.

evidence.text: Section 5.5 and Table 3 define early-termination visit mapping and treatment of unmapped data.

requirement: Do not impute missing outcome values apart from visit mapping; set a derived scale total to missing whenever any required component item is missing, while keeping the separate partial-date rules limited to timing classification of adverse events and medications.
acceptable_values: scale total missing if any item missing
partial-date rules only for timing classification

evidence.text: Section 5.6 distinguishes outcome missingness, scale totals and partial-date imputation.

requirement: Use descriptive analyses rather than a confirmatory hypothesis test: report n, mean, median, standard deviation, standard error, minimum and maximum for continuous variables and participant or event counts and percentages for categorical variables.
acceptable_values: n mean median SD SEM minimum maximum

evidence.text: The protocol limits statistical treatment to descriptive summaries.
Section 5.1 enumerates the descriptive statistics.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy variable as central-video-rater AIMS dyskinesia total score, the sum of items 1-7, and summarize observed values and Day-minus-1 changes at Day -1, Week 8 and Week 52 with two-sided 95% confidence intervals for change.

evidence.text: The protocol defines blinded central AIMS scoring at Day -1, Week 8 and Week 52 or early termination.
Section 5.18 defines the primary efficacy variable, total and summaries.

requirement: Classify AIMS response separately at Weeks 8 and 52 as at least a 50% reduction from the Day-minus-1 central-rater AIMS items 1-7 total and report the responder percentage by dose-trajectory group.

evidence.text: Section 5.18.2.4 defines the visit-specific AIMS responder and displays.

requirement: Summarize CGI-TD categories and 1-to-7 scores at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48 and 52, with separate responder definitions of score 1-2 and score 1-3.

evidence.text: The protocol names CGI-TD and its scheduled visits.
Section 5.18.3 defines scoring, summaries and both responder rules.

requirement: Summarize PGIC categories and 1-to-7 scores at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48 and 52, with separate responder definitions of score 1-2 and score 1-3.

evidence.text: The protocol names PGIC and its scheduled visits.
Section 5.18.4 defines scoring, summaries and both responder rules.

requirement: Derive TDIS total as the sum of items 1-11, set it missing if any item is missing, summarize observed values and change from Day -1 through Week 52 with two-sided 95% confidence intervals, and present AMBMTD only in a participant listing.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies TDIS and AMBMTD assessments and schedule.
Sections 5.18.5-5.18.6 define the TDIS total, summaries and AMBMTD listing.

requirement: Calculate dose compliance as estimated doses taken divided by expected dosing days, classify at least 80% as compliant, and summarize by visit and over treatment through Week 48, using last-attended-visit data for participants lost to follow-up.
acceptable_values: doses taken divided by expected dosing days
last attended visit for lost follow-up

evidence.text: Sections 5.14.1-5.14.2 define dose-count estimation, denominator and compliance classification.

requirement: Summarize NBI-98854 and NBI-98782 plasma concentrations descriptively by visit and most recent dose, stratify CYP2D6 poor versus non-poor metabolizers, set BLQ concentrations to zero and include geometric mean and geometric coefficient of variation.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies scheduled plasma collection for parent and active metabolite.
Section 5.17 defines PK summaries, strata, BLQ handling and additional statistics.

requirement: Tabulate TEAEs by MedDRA system organ class and preferred term with both event count and unique-participant incidence, separating the common 40-mg period through Week 4, the post-Week-4 treatment period, posttreatment and combined intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol includes adverse events in safety monitoring.
Section 5.19.1.1 defines coding, counting units and study intervals.

requirement: Provide overall incidence summaries for any TEAE, related TEAE, severe TEAE, discontinuation-causing TEAE, serious TEAE and fatal TEAE, plus separate listings for deaths, serious events and discontinuation events.

evidence.text: Sections 5.19.1.2 and 5.19.1.4 specify overall incidence categories and event listings.

requirement: Summarize C-SSRS and movement or psychiatric safety scales using their source-defined totals and disease-category restrictions, including BARS, SAS, PANSS, CDSS, YMRS and MADRS; do not combine inapplicable disease strata.

evidence.text: The protocol enumerates suicide, movement and disease-specific psychiatric scales.
Sections 5.19.2-5.19.8 define scale summaries, totals and disease strata.

requirement: Summarize vital signs, triplicate ECG measures including QTcF and clinical laboratories as observed values and changes, identify potentially clinically significant abnormalities using the SAP thresholds, and distinguish treatment from posttreatment periods.

evidence.text: The protocol requires vital-sign, ECG and laboratory safety monitoring.
Sections 5.19.10-5.19.12 define summaries, ECG aggregation, study intervals and PCS thresholds.
